correctness.rationale: Wick expansion reduces the deficit to \(\Delta=2S+8P\). The elliptope determinant gives \(P\ge(S-1)/2\), arithmetic-geometric mean gives \(P\ge-(S/3)^{3/2}\), and the bounds cross only at \(S=3/4\). Explicit equal-magnitude frustrated and rank-two Gram families attain the two branches for every feasible \(S\); equality conditions follow from the equality cases of the two inequalities. The packaged checker independently stress-tests the formulas, but finite checks are not used as proof.

value.rationale: A published quantitative-GPI paper explicitly asks for a three-dimensional quantitative version. The result gives an exact best function, not just a positive remainder, for the fundamental square-product case; it classifies all branch extremizers, identifies a genuine transition at \(S=3/4\), and yields the sharp global stability constant \(2/3\). This is a natural structural refinement tied directly to the dependence geometry of Gaussian triples.
